cards.already: Mixed Kenney has 36 body silhouettes for 44 actors, including eight shared pairs. Standalone 1-Bit already has 44 distinct actor silhouettes. Micro's complete character bodies are all assigned.
cards.decisions: Review individual replacements. The nine Tiny candidates are complete figures, but each needs a suitable identity; they are not nine automatically appropriate new classes. Bastion Bulwark's current Micro #30 looks like a column and is a particularly useful replacement review.
cards.idea: Use spare Tiny Dungeon bodies to separate existing enemies, minibosses and player classes that still share Micro artwork. This is the cheapest useful application of the surplus.

onebit.label: Unassigned figure alternatives; current 1-Bit bodies already differ

cards.title: Give existing enemies more distinct bodies

cards.already: Seven biomes, room families, mushrooms, trees, pillars, rails and ore already exist. These are more precise art variants for existing places, not new mechanics. The standalone look currently shares its base terrain material across the seven biomes.
cards.decisions: Choose each biome’s art palette and decide which wall or prop owns a decoration. Bookcases are objects or wall dressing, not floor textures. The previously declined 1-Bit #315–317 hanging-slime shapes are not proposed as replacement mushrooms.
cards.idea: Dress existing Archive rooms with bookshelves and add matching architectural landmarks. Preserve the currently approved fungal/tree art and collision geometry.
cards.title: Make current biomes easier to recognise

cards.already: Ring of Reversal already uses Micro #89 / 1-Bit #337. The remaining 1-Bit #338–340 are unused. The earlier review interpreted these as rings, explicitly rejecting the bomb interpretation.
cards.decisions: Decide whether Expanding Sigil, Pulse Step or another existing boon benefits from a ring icon. Leave the approved Reversal ring binding intact unless you choose a replacement.
cards.idea: Review spare ring motifs for existing circular/protective boon icons. This is an art alternative, not another new boon or equipment system.
cards.title: Use the spare ring art for existing boon identities

cards.already: Ore already breaks for gold, enemies drop food/health, and barricades are breakable. The earlier volatile-bomb concept was rejected; more break-for-gold objects would add little mechanical variety.
cards.decisions: Choose decoration versus a finite supply cache and agree its effect on resource pacing. Keep the rejected ring-as-bomb and fireplace-as-fuse readings out of the assignments.
cards.idea: Use spare containers as optional scenery or art variants for approved supply/loot objects. Explosive-barrel behavior is not part of this suggestion.
cards.title: Spare barrels, crates and container dressing

cards.already: Gold-paid three-choice chests, food/health drops, ward flasks, shrine room templates and automatic stat growth already exist. There is no implemented HP-payment altar interaction.
cards.decisions: Agree the HP cost and reward quality, whether payment can be lethal, confirmation and one-use rules. Avoid making a mandatory route depend on paying HP. A free healing fountain would overlap existing supplies more strongly.
cards.idea: An optional font offers a boon choice in exchange for a clearly stated HP cost. It adds a risk/reward decision using the current run's frozen boon pool.

onebit.label: Vessel and urn alternatives; not a custom altar illustration

cards.title: One-use offering font

cards.already: Chests, ambushing Vault Lurkers, secrets and locked attacks exist. A chest-to-enemy state transition is new; it should have a tell and a distinct reward outcome. The existing wild-card vault can already spawn an ambush; a haunted cache is only worthwhile if waking and fighting the container itself feels different.
cards.decisions: Choose the warning/tell, wake trigger, reward and disguise rules. HP bars and minimap presentation must match the chosen tell. Keep state and rewards stable through saves; no immediate free ambush damage.
cards.idea: A visibly suspicious cache wakes into an enemy when approached or attacked, then commits an ordinary readable attack. Tiny #92 reads as an open, mimic-like chest; standalone can use a chest-to-ghost transformation with its existing native motifs.

kenney.label: Chest forms, including mimic-like open Tiny #92, plus ghost alternative

cards.title: Haunted cache / mimic encounter

cards.already: Glass Charger moves itself after a strike; Hookrunner pulls an enemy; ordinary brutes sweep. An enemy pushing the player is not currently implemented.
cards.decisions: Approve the creature identity and blocked-landing behavior. Existing public displacement targets AI actors, so player displacement needs deliberate support. Keep attack cells locked; reject occupied/wall landings and unintended floor transitions.
cards.idea: A heavy enemy telegraphs a shove that can move the player one legal tile toward brambles, bog or snares. Its value is positional pressure alongside existing squads.

kenney.label: Blocky golem-like figure or heavy humanoid alternative

onebit.label: Antenna/insect-like body or armoured figure; motif matches need approval

cards.title: A heavy rammer that shoves the player

cards.already: Mend Acolyte/Cinder Mender heal living allies; Forge Conjurer summons; Ward Weaver protects guards; captains rally followers. None currently revives a dead ally.
cards.decisions: This needs corpse records, a once-only budget, legal occupancy checks, cancellation, save continuation and an XP/drop policy that prevents farming. More work than another heal or summon variant.
cards.idea: A vulnerable caster can channel one revival of a fallen squad member. Killing the caster or occupying the locked revival cell prevents it. A finite resurrection budget keeps the fight bounded.

kenney.label: Unused hooded figure alternatives; identity needs review

cards.title: Finite reanimator + corpse counterplay

cards.already: The game has seven two-floor biomes with three-stage routing and unique minibosses. Adding a biome requires route, generation, encounters, boss/reward, persistence and art decisions; tiles alone do not supply those rules.
cards.decisions: Pick its signature mechanic and route role before implementing. Grave/column/door pieces are props or assemblies; choose actual floor and connected-wall materials separately. This is an art-ready theme direction, not a complete approved biome kit.
cards.idea: There is enough grave, bone, ghost and structural artwork for a coherent crypt theme in both looks. A finite resurrection source or another approved distinctive rule could anchor its encounters.

onebit.label: Graves, ghost, bone/staff and skull motifs

cards.title: Crypt / ossuary as a possible eighth biome

cards.already: Current text uses a TTF and panels/meters are drawn in code. These are optional presentation improvements rather than new gameplay. The sheet does not supply a complete uppercase-and-lowercase font workflow.
cards.decisions: Choose a readable subset, metrics/fallback and scalable borders. Keep complete sentences readable and validate multiple viewport sizes. Frame fragments require assembly; card faces do not imply a card-game mechanic.
cards.idea: The shared 1-Bit source has unused borders, arrows, numerals and uppercase glyphs usable in either selectable look. They could supply a focused HUD/menu skin or small numerical fields.

kenney.label: Shared source: frames, digits and arrows

onebit.label: Same unused source cells, usable independently

cards.title: Sprite frames, numbers and a shared visual vocabulary

prior_decisions.detail: Mushroom scenery was approved; a hittable mist-emitting pod was declined. #315–317 were read as hanging slime, not accepted mushrooms.
Micro #89 and 1-Bit #337–340 were read as rings. #570 was read as a fireplace. Spare barrels do not reverse the rejection.
Abandoned mine-rail scenery was approved. No moving cart mechanic was selected.
Micro #123 was excluded from the flask choice; 1-Bit #740 was excluded from the brazier choice. They remain unused art, not approved replacements.

scope: Unassigned art in the two current native Kenney choices. Visual readings, not official Kenney names or approved gameplay.
